answers.answer: Top to bottom: 1 randomly dealt card from the shuffled Conflict I tier, then 5 randomly dealt from the shuffled Conflict II tier, then all 4 Conflict III cards in shuffled order. Shuffle each tier before dealing; return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘1 card ... Conflict I; 5 ... Conflict II; all 4 Conflict III’; unused cards return to box without looking.

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader and the Swordmaster (third Agent) beside the board; 12 troops total, with 3 in the garrison and 9 in supply; 1 water; one cube at the bottom of each of four Influence tracks. Starting VP is 0 in a three-player game and 1 in a four-player game.
answers.evidence: Setup: two Agents; third Agent Swordmaster; 3 troops in garrison and rest in supply; 1 water; cubes on bottom spaces; Score track 1 in 4-player, otherwise 0.

answers.answer: Yes, a Reveal turn is optional even with Agents remaining. After Revealing, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn. Plot Intrigue may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turns, but not after your Reveal turn in that phase.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: may take Reveal while Agents remain; after Reveal, turns are skipped for rest of phase. Plot cards during own Agent or Reveal turns.

answers.answer: Play one card from hand with a matching Agent icon, choose one icon, and send exactly one Agent to an unoccupied space. A card without an Agent icon cannot be used for an Agent turn. Meet the space requirements and pay its costs immediately before resolving any space or card effects; if unable to pay, you cannot enter.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: one card, one Agent icon, unoccupied space; costs and requirements paid immediately before effects.

answers.answer: No. You must pay the space entry cost before resolving the card’s Agent box, so gaining spice from that card cannot fund Conspire when you have only 3 spice against its 4-spice cost. After legal entry and payment, resolve the space effect, Agent box, and Faction Influence advancement in any order.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: costs paid before any effects; effects then gained in any order. Conspire costs 4 spice.

answers.answer: Maximum deployment is 5: all 3 troops recruited this turn (2 from the space and 1 from the card), plus up to 2 from the garrison. Undeployed recruits remain in the garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its recruits go to the garrison and cannot normally be deployed then.
answers.evidence: Deploying: recruits from any source this turn plus up to two more garrison troops; Rally Troops explicitly is not a Combat space.

answers.answer: Reveal all remaining hand cards; resolve only those cards’ Reveal boxes in any order; set Combat strength; then Clean Up by putting all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn steps 1–4; Reveal boxes are of cards just revealed, not Agent-turn cards; Clean Up puts all cards from Agent and Reveal turns in discard.

answers.answer: Yes, after acquiring a card the Imperium Row refills immediately, so you may buy its replacement if affordable. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for a card and split one source across cards. Leftover Persuasion is lost; acquired cards go to discard and cannot be used immediately. An Acquire effect happens once at the moment of acquisition.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: row refills immediately; may pool/split; Persuasion cannot be saved; acquired cards go to discard and are not used right away; Acquire box occurs at acquisition.

answers.answer: 3 troops are 6 strength and 4 swords add 4, for 10 total. If the last troop is removed, strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased, including by swords. Above 20, flip the Combat marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Each Conflict troop = 2; each revealed sword = 1; no troops means strength 0; over 20 use +20 side and restart track.

answers.answer: Starting with the First Player and going clockwise, each player with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass. A pass earlier does not bind later turns. Resolve Combat once all involved players pass consecutively. Play ‘when you win’ cards only after winning, before the next phase.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: turn order, at least one troop, any number or pass; may act after earlier pass; consecutive passes resolve; win-trigger timing stated.

answers.answer: With A and B tied for first, nobody wins; each takes the second reward. C and D still compete for the third reward, which C gets by having higher strength. A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward, including in 2- and 3-player games; a tie for third gives nothing. A player at 0 strength gets no reward. After rewards, troops return to supply.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: first-place tie means second reward each and other two compete for third; second tie gets third reward; third tie nothing; 0 strength no reward; troops go to supply.

answers.answer: Normal Agent-space harvesting happens when the Agent turn resolves: Imperial Basin gives 1 spice plus accumulated bonus, Hagga Basin 2 plus bonus, and The Great Flat 3 plus bonus. At Phase 4 Makers, after Combat, add 1 spice to each Maker space with no Agent. If an Agent moved away and the space is empty in Makers, it gets bonus spice then.
answers.evidence: Board space table lists harvest values; Makers phase checks The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, Imperial Basin; empty space gets 1 spice; Maker clarification says moved-away Agent leaves it eligible.

answers.answer: Reaching 10 VP mid-round does not end the game immediately; check at end of the round in Recall. If the Conflict Deck is empty, that also triggers the end at Recall. Players first resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then most VP wins. Tiebreak order: spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Scoring: trigger at end of round; Endgame Intrigue cards resolve first; listed full tiebreak order.

answers.answer: The VP at 2 Influence is lost if you drop below 2 and regained if you reach 2 again. The bonus earned at 4 is kept after dropping below 4 and can be earned again by re-advancing. First to 4 takes the Alliance; an opponent must rise above the holder to take it by advancement—merely tying does not transfer it.
answers.evidence: Influence and Alliances: 2 VP lost below 2; 4 bonus retained and may be earned again; Alliance first at 4 and transfers only when opponent rises higher.

answers.answer: If the tied holder loses 1 Influence, a previously tied player takes the Alliance; if several were tied, the holder chooses one. If you were the only player at 4 and fall to 3, you lose the token and it returns to the board if nobody else has 4 or more.
answers.evidence: Alliances: previously tied player takes token when holder loses Influence; holder chooses among several; falling to 3 or less returns it if no other player has 4+.

answers.answer: Discarding normally means a card from your hand and puts it in your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from hand, discard pile, or play to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or directed to trash itself. You cannot reshuffle early just to inspect a top card of an empty deck.
answers.evidence: Trashing cards and Deck exhaustion sections state eligible zones/destinations, optionality, and no early reshuffle.

answers.answer: A controller of Arrakeen or Carthag gets 1 Solari whenever any player visits; Imperial Basin’s controller gets 1 spice on any visit. Winning the matching Conflict lets you place your Control marker, replacing an opponent’s. If a later matching Conflict is revealed while you control that space, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Control: winning places/replaces marker; controller receives visit bonus; when a matching Conflict is revealed you may deploy one supply troop.

answers.answer: For setup, use an unused color, put one cube at the bottom of each Influence track, leave all remaining cubes in supply with no troops in its garrison, remove the three ‘1P’ Arrakeen cards, shuffle the remaining House Hagal deck, and place its three Agents near its supply. It takes one Agent turn after each First Player Agent turn, if it has an Agent available, up to three per round; it never Reveals. It gains no resources, VP or Conflict rewards and cannot claim Control, but can hold Alliances. It receives no Influence-track bonuses or Signet Ring effects.
answers.evidence: Two-player setup and Rival sections specify components, turns, no Reveal, resources/rewards/VP/control, Alliances and bonus/signets.

answers.answer: If the indicated space is occupied, reveal another card until an eligible unoccupied space appears. If the deck is empty or a Reshuffle card appears, reshuffle immediately and continue. Ignore normal space costs, requirements and effects; resolve only card icons/instructions. Recruit from Rival supply; on a Combat space deploy recruited troops plus automatically up to two from garrison (one if only one, none if empty), otherwise recruits go to garrison. Harvest Spice chooses the Maker space with most bonus spice, breaking ties by total spice; if no bonus spice exists, draw another card and leave harvested bonus spice removed to the bank. A two-space card uses only the applicable option; if that option is occupied, draw another card and do not switch options.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Agent turns, recruitment/deployment and Harvest Spice rules state these procedures.

answers.answer: If Hagal has a troop in the Conflict, at start of Combat reveal a Hagal card (reshuffle and reveal again if it is Reshuffle), add only its sword icons to 2 strength per deployed troop, then humans may play Combat Intrigue. Hagal occupies its rank but receives no reward. If it wins a Conflict for a space a human controls, remove that human’s Control marker; Hagal does not replace it. Human second-place ties get the third reward even in two-player games, while an ordinary third-place finisher gets nothing.
answers.evidence: House Hagal combat procedure and reward/control rules; tie summary states second-place tie reward.

answers.answer: At Round Start, reveal the top Conflict card and each player draws 5 cards. In ordinary Recall, if no end is triggered, return the Mentat to its space, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and start the next round. A Sort Through the Chaos winner takes the Mentat at the start of the next round.
answers.evidence: Round Start, Phase 5 Recall and official FAQ timing describe these steps.

answers.answer: Solari, spice and water tokens are not limited; substitute if the bank runs out. Troop cubes are different: if your supply is out, you cannot recruit more until some return.
answers.evidence: Setup: resource tokens are not limited; Recruiting: if supply is out of troops, cannot recruit more until some return.

answers.answer: A Leader’s ordinary unique ability works as described on that Leader; its Signet Ring ability activates when you play your Signet Ring card on one of your Agent turns. Card text can override the usual rules.
answers.evidence: Overview: two Leader abilities and Signet Ring timing; cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: Sietch Tabr is a City space with no Faction icon, requires at least 2 Fremen Influence, recruits 1 troop and gives 1 water. It is a Combat space, so troops may be deployed there. You cannot enter at 1 Influence and use the card effect to reach 2 because entry requirements must be met before effects resolve.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table and Combat-space list; Agent turn requires paying/meeting requirements before effects.

answers.answer: Combat spaces are Arrakeen, Carthag, Sietch Tabr, Research Station, Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, The Great Flat, Heighliner, Hardy Warriors and Stillsuits. Research Station and The Great Flat are Combat spaces; Conspire is not.
answers.evidence: Complete list of Combat spaces; Conspire is specifically named among spaces that do not normally allow deployment.

answers.answer: Wealth: no cost; +1 Emperor Influence and 2 Solari. Conspire: 4 spice; +1 Emperor Influence, 5 Solari, recruit 2 troops, draw Intrigue. Foldspace: no cost; +1 Spacing Guild Influence and acquire a Foldspace Reserve card. Heighliner: 6 spice; +1 Spacing Guild Influence, recruit 5 troops, gain 2 water. Secrets: no cost; +1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw Intrigue, and each opponent with 4+ Intrigue gives one chosen at random. Selective Breeding: 2 spice; +1 Bene Gesserit Influence, trash one card to draw two. Stillsuits: no cost; +1 Fremen Influence and 1 water. Hardy Warriors: 1 water; +1 Fremen Influence and recruit 2 troops.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table lists each cost, effect and Faction Influence.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: no cost; recruit 1 and draw a card; its controller gains 1 Solari. Carthag: no cost; recruit 1 and draw Intrigue; its controller gains 1 Solari. Research Station: 2 water; draw 3 cards. Secure Contract: no cost; gain 3 Solari. Imperial Basin: no cost; gain 1 spice plus bonus spice; its controller gains 1 spice. Hagga Basin: 1 water; gain 2 spice plus bonus. The Great Flat: 2 water; gain 3 spice plus bonus. Each Maker space gets 1 bonus spice in Makers if it has no Agent.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table and Makers phase list costs/effects, controller bonuses and bonus spice.

answers.answer: Sell Melange exchanges 2 spice for 6 Solari, 3 for 8, 4 for 10, or 5 for 12; only one exchange per turn. It is a Spice Trade icon space.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table lists rates and one exchange; Spice Trade spaces list includes Sell Melange.

answers.answer: High Council costs 5 Solari, once per game; after placement, you gain 2 Persuasion during each Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Swordmaster costs 8 Solari, once per game; you gain your third Agent and place it on your Leader, with three Agents available for the rest of the game including that round.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table lists costs, once-per-game restriction and when benefits apply.

answers.answer: Hall of Oratory has no cost: recruit 1 troop, and gain 1 Persuasion on your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Rally Troops costs 4 Solari and recruits 4 troops to your garrison (not a Combat space). Mentat costs 2 Solari and draws a card; if Mentat is there, take it to your Leader and use it as an Agent this round, then return it during Recall.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table states all three costs and effects.

answers.answer: Yes. Return the recalled Agent to your Leader and you may use it on another Agent turn that same round. It cannot reopen turns after you have Revealed.
answers.evidence: Recall effects: return Agent to Leader; reusable same round; does not reopen turns after Reveal.

answers.answer: Fremen Bond works during the Reveal turn if you have at least one other Fremen card in play, including a Fremen card played on an Agent turn. Agent-turn and Reveal cards remain face up in play until Clean Up unless trashed; two Bond cards activate one another regardless of order.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond clarification states timing, duration and mutual activation.

answers.answer: A single gain-two-Influence effect cannot be split between Factions. An Alliance icon requires that you hold that Faction’s Alliance token; an Influence-requirement icon requires at least the stated Influence with that Faction.
answers.evidence: Conditional icons: Alliance and Influence requirements; single gain-two effect cannot be split.

answers.answer: Keep Intrigue cards face down, separate from your deck; you may look at them, but reveal only when played. After resolving, discard face up beside the Intrigue deck; if the deck runs out, shuffle discards into a new deck. Plot is playable on your own Agent or Reveal turn, Combat only during Combat, Endgame only at game end. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards section states privacy/destination, timing, reshuffling and that card costs/conditions must be met.

answers.answer: Yes. A delayed Plot such as Charisma or Recruitment Mission can be played on an Agent turn; leave it face up until your next Reveal turn, use its effect then, and discard it.
answers.evidence: Intrigue section explicitly gives Charisma and Recruitment Mission as examples.

answers.answer: A card drawn during your Reveal turn must immediately be revealed and used during that turn, and cannot become an Agent turn. A card drawn after your Reveal turn stays in your hand for next round, when you still draw five additional cards.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn card-draw rule states both cases.

answers.answer: Most board/card effects are mandatory unless they say ‘may,’ use an optional arrow, or optional black-X trash icon; ordinary optional arrow payment/effect may be declined. Board entry costs must be paid, and Intrigue costs/conditions must be met. A non-arrow instruction to trash the card itself is mandatory. An optional arrow effect can be paid and resolved only once, not repeated by paying again.
answers.evidence: Agent turn rules on mandatory effects, arrows, trash icons, entry costs and Intrigue conditions.

answers.answer: Play Bindu Suspension at the start of your Agent turn, before anything else; draw a card, then immediately end your turn.
answers.evidence: Rulebook clarifications: Bindu Suspension timing and immediate end of turn.

answers.answer: No. Calculated Hire can take the Mentat only from its starting position in the Landsraad, not from another player or another board space. For Sort Through the Chaos, the winner takes it at the start of the next round.
answers.evidence: Mentat and Calculated Hire clarifications state location restriction and FAQ timing.

answers.answer: Kwisatz Haderach can take an Agent turn with no unused Agents by sending an Agent already on a board space, even back to that same space. It cannot reuse High Council or Swordmaster and cannot bypass The Voice.
answers.evidence: Kwisatz Haderach clarification states all four restrictions/permissions.

answers.answer: The Voice’s marker is removed on your next turn. It stops opponents, including through Kwisatz Haderach, from sending Agents to the chosen space for one turn. Mark the space with one of your available Control markers.
answers.evidence: The Voice clarification specifies marker, duration and blocked players/actions.

answers.answer: Test of Humanity: opponents choose in order starting from your left and proceeding clockwise; each must choose an action they can actually do. If an opponent discards, that opponent chooses the card, not you and not randomly. The summary gives no rule for Reverend Mother Mohiam’s choice or discard procedure, so that part is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Test of Humanity clarification gives order and legal choices; no Mohiam procedure appears in the summary.

answers.answer: After all setup and before the first round, Baron Vladimir Harkonnen secretly chooses two of four Masterstroke tokens and places them Faction-side down on the Leader; return the other two unseen. Reveal later as described to gain the reward, only once per game. The summary does not specify the detailed reveal timing or method beyond ‘as described,’ so that detail is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Masterstroke clarification states when to choose, hidden placement and once-per-game; reveal ‘later as described’ without details.

answers.answer: Yes. If the Conflict you win rewards spice, take that spice first and use it to pay Demand Respect; To the Victor… can also fund it. A win-trigger Intrigue drawn as a victory reward may be played immediately. A first-place tie has no winner, so a win-trigger card cannot be played for that tie.
answers.evidence: Demand Respect clarification and Combat tie / win-trigger rules.

answers.answer: Yes, ‘any number’ includes zero. Retreating troops move from the Conflict to your garrison; lost troops return to your supply.
answers.evidence: Losing vs. retreating troops clarification.

answers.answer: No. Assassination Mission does not provide a way to trash itself to gain its 4 Solari; another effect must trash it. Imperial Spy draws Intrigue only when its own self-trash effect is used, not when another effect trashes it.
answers.evidence: Assassination Mission / Imperial Spy clarification.

answers.answer: Yes. Keep the VP earned when acquiring The Spice Must Flow even if you later trash that card. Guild Bankers’ discount applies to each copy acquired that turn.
answers.evidence: The Spice Must Flow / Guild Bankers clarification.

answers.answer: Count your The Spice Must Flow cards in your deck and discard pile. The second requirement compares you separately with each opponent: if any one opponent has at least as many as you, you do not meet that requirement.
answers.evidence: Corner the Market clarification states counted zones and opponent-by-opponent comparison.

answers.answer: No. Count Ilban’s Ruthless Negotiator triggers only when paying the printed Solari cost of a board space, not a card ability that costs Solari. Ariana cannot decline Spice Addict; it is mandatory and applies only to spice harvested by sending an Agent to a Maker space, not spice gained by other means.
answers.evidence: Count Ilban / Ariana clarification.

answers.answer: Original base spice is 1 at Imperial Basin, 2 at Hagga Basin and 3 at The Great Flat; bonus spice is separate from base. Liet Kynes counts qualifying cards played on Agent turns this round and cards in the current Reveal turn, for 2 Persuasion each.
answers.evidence: Carryall / Liet Kynes clarification.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire Helena’s set-aside card. You may acquire it by another effect, but the 1-Persuasion discount does not apply that way. If it remains unacquired by the end of your next Reveal turn, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: Helena Richese — Manipulate clarification.

answers.answer: Double Cross requires at least one opponent troop in the Conflict, but does not require a troop in your own supply. Gun Thopter’s Agent box has no effect on an opponent with no garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Double Cross / Gun Thopter clarification.

answers.answer: Shifting Allegiances may lose and gain Influence in the same Faction for a net gain of one, but you must actually pay the loss; a Faction where you have zero cannot pay it. Each Influence track has six spaces; 3 Influence is immediately above the 2-Influence VP space.
answers.evidence: Shifting Allegiances clarification; Faction Influence section gives track size and 3-space location.

answers.answer: Recruitment Mission’s destination choice does not apply to Agent-turn acquisitions. During the applicable Reveal turn, choose independently for each acquired card whether it goes on top of your deck or into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Recruitment Mission clarification.

answers.answer: Refocus reshuffles your deck if your discard pile is empty. Any cards drawn during a Reveal turn must immediately be revealed and used during that turn.
answers.evidence: Refocus / Poison Snooper clarification.

answers.answer: Missionaria Protectiva belongs to Bene Gesserit; after replacing misprints, include only two copies in the Imperium deck.
answers.evidence: Missionaria Protectiva erratum.

answers.answer: Yes. Players can score above 12 VP; the end of the printed Score track is not a limit.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘You can score above 12 VP.’

answers.answer: Rivals are affected by effects targeting opponents or players if they have the specified resources. They gain no Influence-track bonuses and Signet Ring icons have no effect in two-player play.
answers.evidence: House Hagal section states Rival targetability, no track bonuses and no Signet Ring effects.

answers.answer: Hagal acts after each First Player Agent turn, not after the second human’s turns or after a Reveal. It can take up to three turns per round; temporary Mentat or recalled Agents can increase the First Player’s Agent turns and early Revealing can reduce the number. Swordmaster availability affects turns through the First Player’s actual Agent turns, not a fixed two-turn schedule.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Agent turns: after each First Player Agent turn; no fixed two-turn limit; max three Rival turns.

answers.answer: No. Ordinary Persuasion cannot buy Foldspace; acquiring it requires an acquire-Foldspace icon, normally from the Foldspace board space.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards section: Foldspace requires acquire-Foldspace icon and cannot be bought with Persuasion.

answers.answer: You retain City and Fremen icons already on the card. Dispatch an Envoy adds only missing Faction icons and never creates a duplicate, so you do not gain a second Fremen icon.
answers.evidence: Dispatch an Envoy clarification: existing icons remain, including non-Faction icons; no duplicate icon.

answers.answer: Yes. At a Combat space you may deploy any troops recruited that turn from any source, including Plot Intrigue, plus up to two more from your garrison. You cannot count an existing garrison troop as recruited again to evade that limit.
answers.evidence: Deploying rules include recruits from Intrigue and prohibit re-recruiting garrison troops to evade the limit.

answers.answer: Draw the one remaining deck card, then reshuffle the discard pile to form a new deck and continue drawing the other two. Cards still face up in play are not yet in the discard pile, so they do not enter that shuffle.
answers.evidence: Deck exhaustion: when unable to draw, reshuffle discard and continue; Clean Up sends in-play cards to discard later.

answers.answer: Set the board with Mentat on its side in its space and Alliance tokens on the Faction tracks. Build the Conflict deck in three separately shuffled tiers (1 Conflict I, 5 Conflict II, all 4 Conflict III), returning unused cards unseen. Shuffle Intrigue and Imperium decks; deal 5 Imperium cards face up for the Row; set out the three Reserve stacks. Each human chooses/takes a Leader and color, shuffles their 10-card starting deck, starts with 2 Agents and Swordmaster aside, and places score/combat markers and Influence cubes as specified. Set out 3 troops in garrison and 9 in supply, take 1 water, and form the resource bank. Randomly choose the first player and give them the marker; in two-player, also set up Hagal.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–9 describe these deck, board, token, player and first-player preparations.

answers.answer: Unused components in the player’s supply are placed in clear view of all players. Intrigue cards remain face down and are revealed only when played, so their faces are not public.
answers.evidence: Setup: remaining components in clear view; Intrigue section: kept face down and revealed only when played.

answers.answer: You may spend Persuasion before, between, or after resolving Reveal effects; you do not have to finish all Reveal effects first.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn step 2: acquire cards before, between, or after Reveal effects.

answers.answer: City: Arrakeen, Carthag, Sietch Tabr and Research Station. Landsraad: High Council, Swordmaster, Hall of Oratory, Rally Troops and Mentat. Spice Trade: Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, The Great Flat, Secure Contract and Sell Melange.
answers.evidence: Agent icons section enumerates the City, Spice Trade and Landsraad spaces.

answers.answer: The First Player takes the first Phase 2 turn, then play proceeds clockwise one turn at a time. Each turn is either an Agent turn or a Reveal turn; players generally use Agents until out, but may Reveal early. After Revealing, that player is skipped; the phase ends when all players have Revealed.
answers.evidence: Player Turns section states starting player, clockwise turns, optional early Reveal and phase end condition.

answers.answer: At strengths 8, 6 and 4, the 8-strength player wins and takes the top reward; 6 takes the second reward; 4 receives nothing because ordinary third-place reward is only available in a four-player game. In a four-player game, an ordinary third-place finisher receives the third reward.
answers.evidence: Combat resolution: first/top, second/second, ordinary third reward in 4-player only.

answers.answer: At the start of Combat, if Hagal has at least one troop in the Conflict, reveal its combat card and add the sword bonus; then humans may play Combat Intrigue cards. If Hagal has no troop in the Conflict, it gets no combat-bonus card reveal.
answers.evidence: Hagal combat strength procedure conditions reveal on at least one troop, then says humans may play cards.

answers.answer: Corner the Market scores its requirements independently: 1 VP for having at least two The Spice Must Flow cards, and 1 VP for having more than each opponent. It can award 1 VP if only one requirement is met, 2 VP if both are met, and 0 if neither is met.
answers.evidence: Corner the Market clarification states two independent one-VP conditions and outcomes.

answers.answer: Yes. Sardaukar Legion’s Reveal box can deploy up to 3 troops from your garrison during Reveal effects; resolve it before setting strength, so they count immediately.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn notes no normal deployment but card exceptions; Sardaukar example specifies up to three from garrison before strength.

answers.answer: Landsraad Popularity discounts the entry cost of a Landsraad (green) board space by 1 Solari when Leto sends an Agent there; apply the discount before paying to enter. Prudent Diplomacy optionally pays 1 spice for 1 Influence with a Faction where an opponent has more Influence than Leto. A faction where no opponent is ahead is ineligible.
answers.evidence: Duke Leto clarification states category, amount, timing and Prudent Diplomacy condition.

answers.answer: Harvest Spice chooses the Maker space with the most bonus spice; ties are broken by total spice (base plus bonus). If no space has bonus spice, reveal another House Hagal card. Remove the bonus spice from the chosen space and return it to the bank; Hagal does not accumulate resources.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Harvest Spice rules state selection, tie break, no-bonus action and destination.

answers.answer: Allocate Machinations’ first-place ‘Choose two’ reward to two different Factions, gaining 1 Influence in each. You cannot put both into one Faction as with a generic gain-two-Influence effect.
answers.evidence: Conditional icons clarification distinguishes Machinations: choose two different Faction gain-one icons.

answers.answer: Choose one effect for a Master Tactician play: 3 swords or retreat up to 3 troops. You cannot take both. Retreated troops return from the Conflict to your garrison.
answers.evidence: Intrigue section says OR means choose one; Master Tactician example; retreat destination clarification.
